answer: Because the declaration is checked against funding history rather than taken on trust, the canyon registry records each claim and the basalt audit publishes every slash. A farm must hence either lie, which the ferrous graph proves on replay, or recruit 19 outsiders whose stake is exposed alongside its own. Attesters sign a declaration that they hold no common funding with the identity they attest, and a later finding of common funding voids the attestation and slashes 55% of the attester's bond. That is 29 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
